thread:
sylvia (product): quick sync — brightbank escalated: embedding calls on dedicated showing 3-5x latency spikes vs baseline. sales asked for a prioritized fix. can we triage hotfix vs next release?
ev an (sales): customer is on dedicated, committed monthly capacity. they're seeing impact in search relevance and are pushing for a fix before their Monday launch. quoted as P1 by the account exec.
devon (support): logs attached: `embed-svc` tail shows repeated `KV cache miss` followed by longer GPU queues. spikes correlate with 99th percentile seq_len jump from 256->1024.
aisha (eng): thanks. initial thought: workload shift increases KV memory pressure which makes our runtime fall back to slower codepath. quick mitigation candidates: 1) force a model variant with smaller context, 2) enable aggressive prefix/KV eviction, 3) route traffic to a compatible fallback model (lower perf but stable).
sylvia (product): can we estimate effort & risk for a hotfix that toggles eviction policy + routing? want canary plan & acceptance criteria.
aisha (eng): eviction toggle is low effort (config + flags) — low risk, ~4-6h dev + testing. routing rule change is also small but needs careful capacity checks. model variant pinning requires model onboarding checks — higher risk.
evan (sales): customer prefers a quick fix even if slightly different embedding scale; they can re-run a small eval. priority: minimize outage and avoid full release cycle before Monday.
marco (customer-success): they will accept a short canary and a temporary score shift. wants comms to explain degradation window and rollback plan.
amber oncall-bot: Incident created -> INC-20277; severity: elevated. assigned: eng-oncall.
sam (eng-sre): for canary we can route 10% traffic to the eviction-enabled runtime in their dedicated pool. monitoring: token latency, gpu queue length, embedding similarity drift. set alerts at +30% beyond baseline.
aisha (eng): plan: implement `runtime.eviction_policy=aggressive` flag, enable for 10% canary, run for 2 hours, evaluate latency P50/P95/P99 and search quality on the provided prompt set. If stable, roll to 50% then 100% over next day. Rollback is instant by toggling flag.
sylvia (product): acceptance criteria: P99 latency <= baseline *1.25 AND no more than 5% regression in top-5 search precision on customer's eval set. If either fails, rollback immediately. Also need comms template for customer & internal.
evan (sales): customer comms draft: "We will run a targeted change to runtime caching in your dedicated pool; we'll start with 10% of traffic for validation, then expand. Expected risk: minor score drift; rollback available. We'll update in 2 hours and again after full validation."
devon (support): internal comms: slack incident channel with continuous updates every 30m + PagerDuty for SRE. Add ticket to postmortem queue.
aisha (eng): I can push the feature branch and a deploy tag within 6 hours. will need test run in staging with synthetic seq_len bursts.
sam (eng-sre): I'll prepare canary deployment script: `deploy_canary --env=dedicated --customer=brightbank --percent=10 --flag=eviction=aggressive` and a quickcheck that runs the eval harness.
sylvia (product): decision: proceed with hotfix canary. owners: aisha (eng) implement, sam (sre) deploy, devon (support) coordinate comms, evan/marco own customer updates. deadline: start canary within 6h, initial report within 3h of canary start.
evan (sales): noted — i'll schedule the 10:00am check-in with the customer.
marco (customer-success): i'll prepare the bullet comms and blow-by-blow update template.
aisha (eng): quick note for runbook: steps to rollback -> `runtimectl set-flag eviction_policy=default` then `deploy_sync --customer-pool`. test steps: run 200 synthetic high-seqlen requests and compare P99.
sylvia (product): post-deploy: add a short-term ticket to product backlog to investigate a longer-term fix (kernel selection heuristics) and a QE eval to catch seq_len regressions.
devon (support): adding to backlog: "seq_len KV miss surge - root cause analysis" with priority P2 after hotfix.
sam (eng-sre): I'll also add an automated canary monitor that simulates long sequences every 4 hours on dedicated customers, so we don't regress silently.
marco (customer-success): customer acknowledged and is fine with the canary plan. they asked for a brief postmortem once resolved.
sylvia (product): great. keep updates in this thread and incident channel. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
